drivingQuestion: May one place cushions under an animal fallen into water on Shabbat?
outcomeNote: Rav's ruling stands: cushions used when feeding is impossible.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְאַמַּת הַמַּיִם — מֵבִיא כָּרִים וּכְסָתוֹת וּמַנִּיחַ תַּחְתֶּיהָ, וְאִם עָלְתָה — עָלְתָה.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Rav Yehuda said» that «Rav said:» With regard to «an animal that fell into an aqueduct, one brings cushions and blankets,» and throws them into the water ditch, «and places them beneath» the animal in the aqueduct. «And if» the animal thereby «emerges, it emerges.»

segments.he: מֵיתִיבִי: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְאַמַּת הַמַּיִם — עוֹשֶׂה לָהּ פַּרְנָסָה בִּמְקוֹמָהּ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא תָּמוּת. פַּרְנָסָה — אִין, כָּרִים וּכְסָתוֹת — לָא!
segments.en: The Gemara «raises an objection» from a Tosefta: With regard to «an animal that fell into an aqueduct» on Shabbat, «one provides it with sustenance in its place so that it will not die.» This implies that providing it with «sustenance, yes,» that is permitted, providing it with «cushions and blankets, no,» that it is prohibited.

segments.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא — דְּאֶפְשָׁר בְּפַרְנָסָה, הָא — דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּפַרְנָסָה. אֶפְשָׁר בְּפַרְנָסָה — אִין, וְאִי לָא — מֵבִיא כָּרִים וּכְסָתוֹת וּמַנִּיחַ תַּחְתֶּיהָ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: This is «not difficult,» as there is room to distinguish between the cases. «This,» the Tosefta in which it was taught that one provides the animal with sustenance, is referring to a case where «it is possible to provide» it with «sustenance. That,» the mishna in which Rav said that one brings cushions and blankets, is referring to a case where «it is impossible to provide» it with «sustenance.» Where «it is possible to provide» it with «sustenance, yes,» he does so. «And if» it is «not» possible to provide it with sustenance, «he brings cushions and blankets and places them beneath» the animal.

segments.he: וְהָא קָא מְבַטֵּל כְּלִי מֵהֵיכֵנוֹ! סָבַר מְבַטֵּל כְּלִי מֵהֵיכֵנוֹ דְּרַבָּנַן, צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וְאָתֵי דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא וְדָחֵי דְּרַבָּנַן.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Does he not,» by placing the cushions and blankets, «negate a vessel’s preparedness?» The cushions and blankets are no longer fit for their designated use on Shabbat, and this negation of their designated use is similar to the prohibited labor of dismantling. The Gemara answers: Rav «holds» that «negating a vessel’s preparedness» is prohibited «by rabbinic law. Causing a living creature to suffer» is «a Torah» prohibition. «And» a matter prohibited by «Torah law comes and overrides» a matter prohibited «by rabbinic law.»
